scope: Owner's explicit seven-tier roast-level taxonomy and exact five-coffee reassignment. Narrowly supersedes only the existing five roast labels and numeric/display lookup compatibility, not the shot model or coffee approval/privacy/identity decisions.

decisions.decision: Use exactly seven Title Case roast levels in increasing darkness: Ultra Light, Very Light, Light, Medium-Light, Medium, Medium-Dark, Dark.
decisions.old_five_meanings: Preserve prior five categories' meanings and initial espresso ratio/time/temperature recommendations; add Ultra Light and Very Light lighter than Light, and use Medium-Light as the renamed equivalent of old Light-Medium.
decisions.aliases: Accept stored historic Light-Medium as equivalent to Medium-Light in caches, historical imports and read-time compatibility. Preserve literal source and original submission text for provenance; do not silently relabel factual historical evidence.
decisions.unknown: Allow no roast level when unverified; do not infer Ultra Light or Very Light from a roaster's reputation, flavor wording or ambiguous roast graphics.
decisions.recommendations: The two new tiers may initially share existing Light priors rather than inventing scientifically precise new numbers; preserve previously established recipe history, successful shot priority and conservative cross-roast confidence.

decisions.decision: Assign Sweet Bloom Hambela to Light, Orinoco Yirgacheffe to Medium-Light, Proud Mary Bavyeyi IV to Very Light, Queen City David Armijos to Very Light, and private Pending Sweet Bloom Wuri to Very Light.
decisions.affected_scope: Exactly four existing Verified coffees and one existing private Pending Wuri proposal. Preserve names, roaster, source provenance, source field_values, coffee and library identity IDs, all shots/ratings/recipes/community projections, Pending status, member ownership, revision controls and audit history.
decisions.provenance: The owner explicitly provided these subjective espresso-oriented category choices; they are member/owner preferences, not claims that each roaster officially uses the seven-tier taxonomy.

rollout_boundary: Update canonical documents and tests first; stage backwards-compatible SQL schema and application code; preserve historic old-roast read compatibility; never write new labels into production until production app can interpret them. Perform controlled source release and scoped audited data reclassification only after all required credit/release/security checks. No new domain, paid service, automatic promotion or backup deletion.
